terms.plain: Valuing a business off what similar listed companies trade at. Gives a minority value, and the peer set does the valuing — so who chose it matters more than the arithmetic.
terms.formal: A relative valuation method applying trading multiples of similar listed companies to a subject company's financial metrics.

terms.plain: Valuing a business as the cash it will produce, discounted for time and risk. Its real value is forcing you to state your assumptions — most of the answer usually comes from the terminal value.
terms.formal: A valuation method computing present value from projected free cash flows and a terminal value, discounted at a rate matched to the cash flow definition.

terms.plain: The value of the whole business, owed to lenders and shareholders together. Equity value plus net debt — so it pairs with profit measures taken before interest.
terms.formal: The aggregate value of a firm's operating assets, equal to equity market value plus net debt and other claims, used with pre-interest earnings measures.

terms.plain: A company's total value (equity plus debt) divided by its EBITDA. The standard shorthand for how expensive a business is.
terms.formal: Enterprise value divided by EBITDA, a capital-structure-neutral valuation multiple permitting comparison across companies with different leverage.

terms.plain: An estimate of what an asset would fetch in an orderly transaction. For private companies it is produced quarterly by the owner — a considered judgement rather than a price someone paid.
terms.formal: The price receivable on selling an asset in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date, estimated where no observable price exists.

terms.plain: Exiting at a higher multiple than you paid. Real money and not an operational achievement — it reflects what the market was willing to pay, so it should be separated in any attribution.
terms.formal: The component of investment return attributable to a change in the valuation multiple between entry and exit, distinct from earnings growth and debt reduction.

terms.plain: Valuing a business off what acquirers actually paid for similar ones. Gives a control value, so it sits above trading comparables by roughly the control premium.
terms.formal: A relative valuation method applying multiples paid in comparable acquisitions, inclusive of control premia and acquirer-specific synergies.

terms.plain: Everything after the explicit forecast, collapsed into one number. Typically 70-80% of a DCF's answer, resting on two assumptions nobody can verify.
terms.formal: The present value at the forecast horizon of all subsequent cash flows, computed as a growing perpetuity or from an assumed exit multiple.

terms.plain: Value divided by a measure of profit. A compressed discounted cash flow: every multiple implies a growth rate, a discount rate and a reinvestment need, without saying which.
terms.formal: A ratio of enterprise or equity value to an earnings, cash flow or revenue measure, used for relative valuation against comparable assets.
